chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Fatima (peace be upon her) lived after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) for seventy-five days. She was not seen smiling nor laughing. She would visit the graves of the martyrs twice every week, on Mondays and Thursdays, saying: 'Here was the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and here were the polytheists.' And in another report, Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that she used to pray there and supplicate until she died (peace be upon her).'
ai.seo_question: How long did Fatima (peace be upon her) live after the Prophet's death and what was her daily routine during this period?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the seventy-five-day period between the Prophet's death and Sayyida Fatima's passing, emphasizing her profound, unceasing grief as evidenced by her lack of laughter. It establishes the spiritual precedent for visiting graves (ziyarat) not merely as mourning, but as a devotional act of connecting with the legacy of the Prophet and the martyrs, a practice central to Shia piety. The narration underscores the continuity of her spiritual presence and devotion until her own death, reinforcing the significance of the grave as a locus of divine remembrance.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Ssaeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Syeda Fatima<sup>asws</sup> lived after Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> for seventy five days, not being seen smiling nor laughing. She<sup>asws</sup> was going to the graves of the martyrs twice very week, the Mondays and the Thursdays, so she<sup>asws</sup> would be saying: ‘Over here was Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and over there were the Polytheists’.
And in another report of Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdullahasws, that Syedaasws used to Pray Salaat over there and supplicated until when sheasws passed away’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Al-Nadr ibn al-Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘Fatimah, ‘Alayha al-Salam, lived for seventy-five days after the death of the Messenger of Allah. During this time, she was never seen laughing or smiling. Every week she would go twice to the gravesites of the martyrs, once on Monday and on Thursdays, and say, ‘There was the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and there were the pagans.”’

In another Hadith, Aban has narrated from those whom he has mentioned from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following: “She would perform salat (prayer) there and pray until she died.”
